sentences.text:
2 The writ petition has been filed in the nature of certiorari seeking interference with the communication dated 08.05.2019 in BOB- ZOSARB :22:132 dated 08.05.2019 issued by the third respondent, Bank of Baroda represented by Chief Manager at Avinashi Road Branch, in Tiruppur and also with respect to a request issued again by the Bank of Baroda now represented by its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer/first respondent dated 30.06.2021 for issuance of a Look Out circular LOC and further circular issued by the fourth respondent/Bureau of Immigration,
Ministry of Home Affairs, New Delhi dated 01.07.2021 in circular No. 1/SIC/(ACK)/LOC/2021- 6209 whereby, the fourth respondent had opened a Look Out Circular as Suspect No. from 2144948 to 2144952 against the petitioner who in the writ petition had given his address as No. 37C,
Chokkakathan Street, Madurai  625001.
2.
The family members of the petitioner herein more particularly his father had been running a family business concern in the name of M/s. Anbu Textiles Private Limited.
It was incorporated in the year 2002.
The petitioner having qualified himself, had resigned as Director https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis from the said Private Limited Company on 28.5.2008.
This is a statement made by the petitioner in the affidavit.
Let me not take it as a gospel truth but record it as the statement made by him.

In support of that particular statement along with a series of documents filed, Form 32 which is to be submitted to the Registrar of Companies whenever there is a change in directorship has also been filed as a document and it also reflects that the petitioner had resigned as a Director on 28.05.2008.
It is however not known as to when this particular Form 32 was actually forwarded to the Registrar of Companies.
There is absolutely no information whether a copy of the same was also forwarded to the officials of the Bank of Baroda.

This is significant because Anbu Textiles, had obtained substantial loan from Bank of Baroda, Avinashi Road Branch/the third respondent herein, and when the loan was sanctioned, the petitioner had been addressed by Bank officials as a Director of Anbu Textiles Private Limited and he had also signed that particular form.
His stand however is that he was only a Guarantor and had extended personal guarantee for the loan.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.

Let me not deal further into the loan aspect primarily because there had been proceedings before the Debt Recovery Tribunal and therefore it is quite evident that the loan had not been repaid and there are substantial amounts due as on date.

It is also evident from the arguments advanced that the property which the petitioner had offered as Guarantee has also been sold during those proceedings and amounts have been realized consequent to such sale.
In the year 2014 or in the year 2015, the petitioner, consequent to his continuous residence at Australia, had been recognized as an Australian Citizen.
The loan however continued to subsist and the respondents particularly, the Bank of Baroda had been taking various steps to recover the amount.
They also categorized the default as willful default.
They had issued a show cause notice prior to that and the same had also been answered by the family members of the petitioner herein.
Still it is a fact that loan had been declared as a willful default.

There was also an earlier occasion when the bank officials had lodged a complaint through email and during the course of arguments, it had been pointed out to me that the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Central Crime Branch at Tiruppur had, on 31.12.2016, examined such complaint which was dated 28.11.2016 against Anbu Textiles and their proprietors and had come to a conclusion that commission of offense https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of criminal breach of trust has not been elicited from a reading of the complaint therein.

sentences.text: The bank was however persistent.
They did not let matters rest at that.

They went forward by filing an application under Section 156 (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the jurisdictional Magistrate and consequent to an order of the learned Magistrate, which order has not been placed before this Court, an FIR in Crime No. 31 of 2018 had been registered on 26.11.2018 by the Sub Inspector of Police, Central Crime Branch at Tiruppur for offences under Section 34 read with 406 and 420 IPC against the company namely Anbu Textiles Private Limited and the petitioner herein who was arrayed as the fourth accused again with address at Madurai and also against his father and two other brothers.
I am informed that the said FIR is still pending.
There is no information given whether consequent to the investigation, a final report had been filed before the Judicial Magistrate or not.
As on date, the only available information to this Court is that the FIR is pending.

It is common knowledge that an FIR is only an information given to the police and though categorized as an accused, such person cannot certainly be categorized as having been convicted for commission of the offense.
Conviction follows trial and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis trial follows final report being filed and final report follows investigation by the police.
None of those steps to the information of this Court have been taken by the jurisdictional police/investigating officer.
5. As stated, however, the bank was still persistent.
They then went forward by issuing a communication seeking to issue a Look Out notice as against the petitioner herein categorizing him as a Director.

Consequent to their request, and based on the expansive nature of powers given under the Circular which was originally issued in the year 2010, wherein in the year 2018, more particularly by an office memorandum on 04.10.2018, a Lookout Circular can also been issued on the request of the Managing Director or the Executive Officer of a public sector bank, the fourth respondent had issued the circular dated 01.07.2021 categorizing the petitioner as one against whom a Look Out Circular is in force.
6. The writ petition is focused as against two particular orders/circulars.
First one is the categorization of the loan as willful default.

Examination of that aspect is beyond the scope of this writ petition and I would very categorically state that insofar as the relief sought with respect to that communication dated 8.05.2019 issued by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the Bank of Baroda, a writ court under Article 226 of the Constitution can never enter into any discussion whether a particular default is willful or not willful.

That would require appreciation and examination of records and it would be beyond the scope of this court to examine that particular aspect and therefore, I would not grant the particular relief sought by the petitioner relating to the Communication dated 08.05.2019.
7. Arguments were advanced by the learned Senior Counsel, Mr. Sathish Parasaran, with respect to the Look Out Circular opened up in the name of the petitioner.
These arguments were countered by Mr. M.S. Krishnan, learned Senior Counsel on behalf of the Bank.

I must appreciate the role of the learned Additional Solicitor General, Mr. ARL. Sundaresan, who presented a balanced view on the facts and presented the circulars which now prevail on the issue herein.

8. The thrust of the arguments of the learned Senior Counsel on behalf of the petitioners is that, the Look Out Circular had been sought for by the Bank authorities with total non-application of mind as A. Aravinthan vs Bank Of Baroda on 19 January, 2023

4 they have overlooked the fact that the petitioner had resigned as a Director with effect from the year 2008 itself.

The Look Out Circulars however https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis still categorized the petitioner as a Director of the Company and it is therefore urged that there was absolute lack of application of mind on that particular aspect.

However, this statement is countered by learned Senior Counsel, Mr. M.S. Krishnan by pointing out that a Look Out Circular can be issued not only to a Director of a Bank but also to any borrower or Guarantor.

The issue with respect to a Guarantor was specifically addressed in the year 2015 but it is pointed out that a Guarantor cannot be so issued with a Look Out Circular but the word also used is 'borrower' and this could very well include in its sweep not only the principal borrower but also a guarantor also.
9. The further issue which came up for consideration is whether as an Australian citizen, the petitioner could be subjected to a Look Out Circular.

It is pointed out that the Circular which emanated from the Office Memorandum dated 27.10.2010 relating to issuance of Look Out notices speaks, not only of Indian citizens but also of Foreign Nationals.

Since it is not specifically called for,
let me not enter into that particular discussion whether the petitioner should be protected from issuance of Look Out Circular only the ground that he is an Australian citizen and not an Indian citizen.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10.
The fact remains that he is a Guarantor.
The facts remains that the loan is still subsisting.
The fact remains that as a Guarantor, his liability subsists so long as the loan subsists and the debt subsists.
11. It is under these circumstances that it has to be examined whether a broader view can be taken with respect to the relief sought by the petitioner herein.
12. It is not in doubt that the petitioner is gainfully employed in Australia.

It has to be further examined whether his presence here is actually required as Mr. M.S. Krishnan, learned Senior Counsel, pointed out for 'negotiations' with the company namely Anbu Textiles for settlement of the loans.

As a person, who is not a Director and therefore not in control of the affairs of the company, it would be a moot question to answer whether the petitioner could influence any decision to be taken by the Directors involving the subsisting loan.
The property which he had offered as collateral security for the loan had already been dealt with and sold and sale proceeds realized.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 13.

Learned Senior Counsel, Mr. M.S. Krishnan relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court K.D. Sharma vs Steel Authority of India Limited and Others reported in (2008) 12 Supreme Court Cases 481 and laid particular emphasis to paragraph No. 34 which is as follows:
 34.

entities.text: K.D. Sharma vs Steel Authority of India Limited and Others reported in (2008) 12 Supreme Court Cases 481
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 and of the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution is extraordinary, equitable and discretionary.
Prerogative writs mentioned therein are issued for doing substantial justice.

It is,
therefore, of utmost necessity that the petitioner approaching the writ cout must A. Aravinthan vs Bank Of Baroda on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135170528/
5 come with clean hands, put forward all the facts before the court without concealing or suppressing anything and seek an appropriate relief.

sentences.text: If there is no candid disclosure of relevant and material facts or the petitioner is guilty of misleading the court, his petition may be dismissed at the threshold without considering the merits of the claim.

14. This preposition was pointed out consequent to the fact that is one of the communications,
though he is an Australian citizen, the petitioner had given his address as being a resident of Madurai.
It is therefore stated that he had misled the bank officers into believing that he is actually in India.
15. It is contended that the petitioner has not come to court with https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis clean hands and therefore this Court should not extend any relief to the petitioner herein.

However,
it is evident that the primarily onus was on the bank officials to determine the status of the petitioner.

The responsibility of the Branch Manager to examine in detail the status of each one of the borrowers or the guarantors to such loans is paramount and cannot be shifted to the guarantors or the borrowers to explain who they are or not are.
The petitioner had never been called upon to disclose whether he is an Indian citizen or not an Indian citizen.
It is a fact that Form 32 is presented as a document before this Court.

It is a fact that in the said document, it is seen that the petitioner has resigned as a Director on 28.05.2008.
16.

Learned Senior Counsel also relied on the observation of a learned Single Judge of the Telengana High Court in W.P.No. 6892 of 2022, Garikapati Venkateswara Rao vs Union of India, Represented by its Secretary, Ministry of Home, New Delhi and Others, wherein the learned Single Judge had examined the judgment of the Supreme Court in Satwant Singh Sawhney vs. D. Ramaratnam,
Assistant Passport Officer, New Delhi reported in AIR 1967 SC 1836, wherein, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had expressed its opinion that no person can be deprived of his right to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis travel except according to the procedure established by law.

Single Judge had also relied on the observation in Menaka Gandhi vs Union of India reported in (1978) 1 SCC 248, wherein again it had been reiterated that no person can be deprived of his right to go abroad unless there is a liability enabling the State to so deprive.

entities.text: Menaka Gandhi vs Union of India reported in (1978) 1 SCC 248
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further reference was also made to a judgment reported in (2018) SCC Online Madras 2229, in Karti P Chidambaram vs. Bureau of Immigration, where again it had been observed that a LOC is dependent upon the circumstances prevailing on the date on which the request of issuance of LOC had been made.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. After examining those observations, the learned Single Judge stated that since the respondent bank in that particular case had initiated recovery proceedings against the petitioner therein and further that if the Look Out Circular is lifted and the petitioner therein disappears, the recovery proceedings would be brought to stand still and recovery of crores of public money would become impossible, therefore justified the issuance of the Look Out notice.
18. In the instant case, the facts will have to be examined.
They https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis are slightly different.
I do not think there is a possibility of petitioner disappearing forever from this world.
His passport No had been declared in the affidavit.
His passport No is PB 5153163.

sentences.text: The petitioner is not directly involved with the affairs of the company.
The petitioner can never participate in negotiations with the bank officials with respect to the loan.
But as guarantor, his property had already been sold.
The Look out notice had been issued only on the basis that petitioner is a Director, which statement is not a correct statement.

In view of these peculiar circumstances, I would issue the following guidelines:
i) The Look out notice in Circular No. 1/SIC/(ACK)/LOC/2021- 6209 dated 01.07.202 issued by the fourth respondent insofar as the petitioner alone is hereby quashed and is set aside.
ii) The petitioner is permitted to go abroad since he is an Australian citizen.

iii ) Before going to abroad, the petitioner must make a visit to the office premises of Bank of Baroda, Avinashi Road Brach, at Tiruppur and disclose his address at Australia and all other contact details in Australia.
iv) After reaching Australia, the petitioner must present https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis himself before the Indian Embassy at the State of his residence in Australia and inform them that if the third respondent/Bank of Baroda whereto ever communicate seeking his presence, he will be ready and willing to come back to India.
Till such time, let him reside in Australia.

20. It is reiterated that the fourth respondent may call for the presence of the petitioner only in case of actual necessity since he is neither a Director nor he is in a position to influence negotiations with the bank.

21. If ever any decree is passed against the petitioner by a competent court of law and execution is enforced against the petitioner in his personal capacity, then the third respondent may inform,
through proper channels, the Embassy officials at Australia wherever the petitioner resides and call upon them to put the petitioner on notice about the decree.
22. I hold that the extreme step of issuing look Out Circular is not required in this particular case.
The petitioner is not a principal borrower, is not the director, is not directly liable for the loan and is https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis not in a position to negotiate for the return of the loan.
He need not be put to agony of being inflicted with a Look Out Circular.
Reasonable restrictions can alone be placed.
Directions can be issued to the petitioner to present himself whenever required by the third respondent.
23. With the above directions, writ petitions stands disposed of sofar as issue of Look Out Circular is concerned.
No costs.
Consequently, connected W.M.P.Nos. 684 and 686 of 2023 is closed.
